citation.source: USDA FoodData Central (fdc.nal.usda.gov), raw potato, flesh and skin
citation.note: Figures are in the range USDA FoodData Central publishes for raw potato — this repo has not looked up the exact current FDC entry/ID to confirm the precise values, and potato composition genuinely varies by cultivar (see garlic.json's cultivar note for the same caveat on a different crop).

citation.source: Choi & Okos (1986), "Effects of Temperature and Composition on the Thermal Properties of Foods" — the standard predictive model in food engineering for deriving thermal conductivity/density/specific heat from a food's composition
citation.note: This repo has not run potato's actual composition through the Choi-Okos model to re-derive these numbers — they're recalled as being in the right range for a starchy tuber, not computed from it here.

metadata.notes: possibleStates/capabilities grounded in CLAUDE_DEV_CTX.md's own potato examples ('cannot peel a potato that is already boiled', INVALID_TRANSITIONS: boiled/fried/mashed). statePrerequisites.cut originally required 'peeled' unconditionally; widened 2026-08-13 to ['washed','peeled'] (see ingredient.ts's array-valued statePrerequisites) so skin-on cuts (rustic wedges, skin-on fries — a real, legitimate style, not an oversight) are representable too, not just the peeled path. boil/fry/bake are three distinct verbs on purpose: cooked in water vs. oil vs. dry heat give different results, so they're not collapsed into one generic COOK verb. mash was NOT wired up for a long time (no 'mash' action existed despite 'mashed' being a listed state) — closed 2026-08-13, see mashNote below. possibleTags/salt: seasoning is orthogonal to possibleStates — a 'salted boiled potato' is state 'boiled' plus tag 'salted' held at once, not a single combined state.
metadata.mashNote: MASH (data/actions/mash.json) + isMashable, closed 2026-08-13 — the single most glaring gap found while auditing this repo's own honesty: 'mashed' had been a listed possibleState since the first potato entity existed, with ZERO action ever producing it, the exact same shape of dead-label gap 'heat as a place' work found in pan.json's unreachable 'hot'/'cold' states. statePrerequisites.mash: ['boiled','baked'] — you cannot mash a raw potato; it must already be cooked soft via one of two real, distinct paths (conventional boiled-then-mashed, or baked-then-scooped for twice-baked). Once mashed, FRY still works on it with ZERO further changes (FRY has no statePrerequisites entry at all) — a mashed potato can be pan-fried directly (a real, simple 'potato cake'/leftover-mash technique), though a true breaded croquette (mash -> shape -> bread/batter -> fry) still can't be fully represented: no coating/breading mechanism exists in this vocabulary (named, not built — same discipline as every other scoped-out gap here).
metadata.gratedNote: GRATE (data/actions/grate.json) + isGratable, added 2026-08-13, for hash browns/rösti — deliberately its OWN verb/tool (grater.json), not a sixth value on CUT's shape enum: a box grater shreds by friction against a grating surface, physically nothing like a knife's slicing motion, and folding it into CUT would have wrongly implied a knife produces grated potato. statePrerequisites.grate: ['washed','peeled'], same either-path reasoning as cut's own prerequisite (skin-on grating for rustic hash browns is a real, legitimate style too). Whether the grated shreds are rinsed/squeezed of surface starch (crispier, more separate hash browns) or left as-is (starch helps bind a rösti into one cake) is a further real technique distinction this schema does not model — same depth limit as everywhere else in this vocabulary.
metadata.combineNote: isCombinableBase + statePrerequisites.combine: 'fried' — tortilla de patatas combines already-fried potato with beaten egg, not raw. See data/actions/combine.json and data/entities/tortilla_mixture.json (the first entity in this repo to actually use structure.composite/components).
metadata.seasoningNote: pepper/chili added to allowedTransformations 2026-08-13 alongside salt, the first entity to use all three seasoning verbs (data/actions/pepper.json, chili.json) — same addsTag/possibleTags mechanism as salt, no recipe currently exercises them (built to make the vocabulary capable, not forced into an existing dish that wasn't asked to have pepper/chili).
metadata.simmerNote: SIMMER (data/actions/simmer.json) added 2026-08-13, isSimmerable alongside isBoilable — reaches the SAME 'boiled' state as BOIL, deliberately (see simmer.json's sharedTransformedStateNote), just via a gentler, lower-turbulence process real technique actually recommends for whole/halved potatoes to avoid broken skins and starch-clouded water. No recipe currently exercises it (same 'capable, not forced in' discipline as pepper/chili above).
metadata.parFryNote: isParFryable + PAR_FRY (data/actions/par-fry.json), added 2026-08-13 in response to a direct question about how shape/size/oil temperature affect fried potato outcome. Unlike SIMMER, PAR_FRY deliberately does NOT reuse FRY's 'fried' transformedState — 'par_fried' is a genuinely different, unfinished intermediate (pale, soft, not crisp), not the same dish reached more gently, so collapsing it into 'fried' would have been the wrong call here even though it was the right call for SIMMER/BOIL (see simmer.json's sharedTransformedStateNote for why that distinction matters and isn't just inconsistency). No statePrerequisites entry added for 'fry' itself — FRY stays callable from any state, same as before, so a direct single-stage fry from 'peeled'/'raw' still works unchanged; PAR_FRY then FRY is an additional, not exclusive, path.
metadata.fryingScienceNote: The real physics behind 'depends on shape, size, oil temperature': Kalogianni & Smith, "Effect of frying variables on French fry properties," International Journal of Food Science and Technology 48(4):758-770 (2013) — https://doi.org/10.1111/ijfs.12024 — found water removal and oil uptake are NOT simply linked (a thicker crust from more water loss did not mean proportionally more oil absorbed), most property change happens in the first 1-2 minutes of frying, and crust thickness plateaus (~0.35-0.46mm) despite continued heat penetration, due to compensatory shrinkage. None of this is modeled numerically here — CUT's 'shape' parameter (data/actions/cut.json) already gives potato a real, distinct piece-size state, but nothing connects that state to FRY's/PAR_FRY's durationSeconds or oilTempC the way a real fryer (or a real cook) would adjust for it. Same informational-only depth limit as every other parameter in this vocabulary (see fry.json's parameterNotes) — named honestly rather than implied solved by PAR_FRY's addition.
